UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, especially Articles 3, 4, 7, 8, 14 and 25; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving its implementing regulation; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership; Law 11/2021 of 9 July amending Law 10/2010 and strengthening beneficial-ownership transparency; relevant corporate-record provisions of the Spanish Companies Act and the Commercial Registry Regulations.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A Spanish Sociedad Limitada must have a registered office in Spain corresponding to the place of effective management or the principal establishment or operation, subject to Companies Act requirements. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for the registered-office function of a holding or administrative company if it provides reliable legal-notice handling, books, records, and access for authorities. It is not sufficient as operational substance for recombinant human insulin manufacturing. Manufacturing requires an appropriately licensed and inspected facility, qualified personnel, quality systems, batch and pharmacovigilance records, storage and distribution controls, and compliance with AEMPS, EU pharmaceutical, GMP, environmental, occupational-safety, and potentially regional-authority requirements.

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (name certification) and the Provincial Commercial Registry of the registered office (Colegio de Registradores de España).

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, 'LSC') — Arts. 19, 20, 22–28 and 62 (S.L. minimum capital €3,000); Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1784/1996); Ley 14/2013 de apoyo a los emprendedores (fast-track incorporation).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarized public deed of incorporation) followed by mandatory inscription in the Registro Mercantil.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 64 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime Mandatory Capital Deposit & Lockup

Statutory minimum share capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash at incorporation. The capital contribution must be deposited in a blocked escrow account at a Spanish credit institution and the corresponding deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) must be presented to the notary; funds are released to the company only upon registration.

Funding & unlock path: Mandatory municipal fire safety certificate based on approved Fire Protection Project (RD 513/2017 and CTE DB-SI); structural load inspection certificate signed by a competent architect/technical architect covering the GMP cleanroom floors and anti-vibration systems; occupational health and safety clearance including a workplace risk prevention plan and health surveillance program run by an accredited external Prevention Service (SPA), plus the pre-operational inspection (acta de comprobación) by the regional health authority prior to the first GMP batch production.

Paid-in capital rule: Statutory minimum share capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash at incorporation. The capital contribution must be deposited in a blocked escrow account at a Spanish credit institution and the corresponding deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) must be presented to the notary; funds are released to the company only upon registration.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Central Registry, Delegación Central de Grandes Contribuyentes, and Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales; official portal www.agenciatributaria.es; coordination with the Registro Mercantil Central for corporate legal registration.

E-government filing portal

An inbound foreign-owned SL obtains its NIF (CIF-equivalent) through a Spanish notary: (1) obtain the negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social) from the Registro Mercantil Central; (2) execute the incorporation deed before a notary; (3) the notary requests the provisional NIF electronically from the AEAT Central Registry (issued instantly, valid 6 months); (4) file the deed at the provincial Mercantile Registry within 2 months (usual completion 4-8 weeks); (5) request the definitive NIF immediately after Mercantile Registry registration (issued electronically, same day). Parallel obligations: register in the Censo de Empresarios before commencing activity (modelo 036/037); obtain an EORI number for customs and export operations; each non-resident shareholder must obtain a Spanish NIF through a legal representative with power of attorney. The definitive NIF is the sole taxpayer identifier for corporate income tax (IS), VAT/IVA, and customs procedures.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — an SL incorporated and registered in Spain is a Spanish tax resident subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) on worldwide income at the general 25% rate, or 15% for a newly created SL in the first two years with a positive taxable base (art. 29.1 LIS 27/2014). No pass-through or check-the-box classification is available under Spanish law. Dividend/participation exemption applies under art. 21 LIS for qualifying holdings. The Canary Islands ZEC special 4% rate is available only in the Canary Islands territorial scope, which does not cover a Peninsular biopharma export platform. — An inbound foreign-owned SL obtains its NIF (CIF-equivalent) through a Spanish notary: (1) obtain the negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social) from the Registro Mercantil Central; (2) execute the incorporation deed before a notary; (3) the notary requests the provisional NIF electronically from the AEAT Central Registry (issued instantly, valid 6 months); (4) file the deed at the provincial Mercantile Registry within 2 months (usual completion 4-8 weeks); (5) request the definitive NIF immediately after Mercantile Registry registration (issued electronically, same day). Parallel obligations: register in the Censo de Empresarios before commencing activity (modelo 036/037); obtain an EORI number for customs and export operations; each non-resident shareholder must obtain a Spanish NIF through a legal representative with power of attorney. The definitive NIF is the sole taxpayer identifier for corporate income tax (IS), VAT/IVA, and customs procedures.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation — an SL incorporated and registered in Spain is a Spanish tax resident subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) on worldwide income at the general 25% rate, or 15% for a newly created SL in the first two years with a positive taxable base (art. 29.1 LIS 27/2014). No pass-through or check-the-box classification is available under Spanish law. Dividend/participation exemption applies under art. 21 LIS for qualifying holdings. The Canary Islands ZEC special 4% rate is available only in the Canary Islands territorial scope, which does not cover a Peninsular biopharma export platform.

Available election forms

Spain has no US-style check-the-box election. Available elections: (i) consolidated tax group regime (régimen de grupos de sociedades) for direct or indirect shareholding of at least 75% (70% for listed groups) held for more than one full tax year, with irrevocable entry for a 3-year period; (ii) reinvestment relief (deducción por reinversión) and equalization reserve (reserva de nivelación) for entities with turnover up to 10,000,000 EUR; (iii) hybrid mismatch adjustments under arts. 15 ter-15 quinquies LIS implementing ATAD 2 — mandatory, not elective; (iv) patent box (art. 23 LIS): 60% reduction on qualifying intangible income, subject to substance and tracing rules — relevant for process IP in recombinant insulin manufacturing; (v) VAT optional cash-basis regime (régimen especial de criterio de caja) for turnover up to 2,000,000 EUR, irrevocable for 3 years — usually unattractive for exporters; (vi) SME VAT exemption under EU Directive 2020/285 with an 85,000 EUR annual turnover cap on domestic supplies, exercisable by notification in the Censo de Empresarios since 1 January 2024 — generally inadvisable for a biopharma exporter because input VAT deduction is lost; (vii) OSS/non-established taxable person registration for intra-community distance sales (10,000 EUR threshold).

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general de minimis turnover threshold: any person carrying out a business activity in Spanish territory must register in the Censo de Empresarios before commencing operations (modelo 036/037). The special SME exemption introduced under EU Directive 2020/285 applies only when annual turnover does not exceed 85,000 EUR for domestic supplies and 10,000 EUR for intra-community distance sales; it must be exercised via the Censo and is not suitable for an exporter with significant recoverable input VAT. A pharmaceutical manufacturer exporting recombinant human insulin must register for VAT regardless of turnover in order to obtain the export exemption and process VAT refunds.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

The full export exemption (exención plena con derecho a deducción) under art. 21.1 Ley 37/1992 applies when goods are dispatched or transported by the seller or a third party on the seller's behalf from Spain/EU territory to a destination outside the EU (excluding the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla). The goods must physically leave EU territory within 3 months from the date of dispatch (art. 21.5 Ley 37/1992). This 0% rate covers exports of recombinant human insulin to sovereign health programs in Latin America using letter-of-credit rails, provided the exporter is VAT-registered in Spain and holds a valid EORI number. Directly ancillary transport, loading, and handling services (arts. 21.18-21.22 Ley 37/1992) are also exempt; separately invoiced insurance and disbursements follow general place-of-supply rules. Input VAT on raw materials, utilities, logistics, and quality-control services used for the exported insulin is fully creditable through the monthly model 303/390 cycle, with refunds processed through the SII-audited route; no special prior export-refund authorization is required beyond standard registration.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo), including the electronic exit confirmation (certificado de salida) generated by the Spanish customs system (TARIC/DEA)
  • Bill of Lading (B/L) for sea freight, Air Waybill (AWB) for air freight, or CMR with electronic customs exit validation for road transport, evidencing departure from Spain/EU to the non-EU destination
  • Commercial invoice stating the Spanish exporter's NIF-VAT and EORI, the foreign purchaser's full details, the recombinant human insulin batch reference, Incoterms (FOB/CIF/EXW), and explicit reference to the art. 21 LIVA export exemption
  • Packing list and, where applicable, the EMA/AEMPS batch-release certificate and certificate of analysis for biologics/pharmaceuticals
  • Payment evidence: SWIFT MT103 or a bank letter-of-credit credit advice under the Sovereign_Health_LC rail, cross-referenced to the invoice number and the export declaration
  • EUR.1 / EUR-MED certificate or REX invoice origin declaration when a preferential origin claim is made in the importing country (non-constitutive for Spanish zero-rating)
  • Freight forwarder instructions and transport operator booking confirmations, retained by the exporter for at least 5 years

(1) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información, RD 596/2016, operative since 1 July 2017): mandatory for large enterprises with turnover above 6,000,000 EUR, VAT groups, and taxpayers in certain special regimes; requires near-real-time submission of issued/received invoice records to AEAT within 4 working days of the accounting entry date, with 8 working days for taxpayers filing annual returns; (2) Verifactu (Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece', art. 12; RD 1007/2023): mandatory integrity and traceability system for all invoice-issuing software; software producers must be compliant by 31 December 2024 and all other taxable persons by 31 December 2025; generates QR-coded, hash-chain-protected electronic invoice records (XML) that must be made available to AEAT on request — not a per-transaction clearance system but an audit-ready fiscal memory; (3) Export customs clearance: electronic filing of the DUA through the AEAT customs window ('Aduanas 24/7' system using TARIC/DEA), with EORI validation required; the SII export book entries must reference the DUA and the date of physical departure; (4) mandatory e-invoicing in B2G relations (Facturae standard is already operational) and future general B2B e-invoicing obligations under Ley 18/2022 are expected to be fully enforced in 2026; SII and Verifactu already provide the functional equivalent for tax control purposes.

AEAT central risk units (ONIF and Customs) target exporters on red flags such as rapid growth of zero-rated exports to high-risk jurisdictions, persistent VAT refund claims without matching production capacity, SII discrepancies between export books and the DUA register, and irregular LC documentation. If the export exemption is denied (goods never left the EU, export completed after the 3-month deadline, or falsified documents), AEAT will: (i) regularize the transaction and assess the omitted output VAT (21% standard rate, or 4% super-reduced rate if recharacterized as a domestic supply of human-use medicines); (ii) disallow input VAT deductions when underlying records are not substantiated; (iii) charge statutory late-payment interest on tax debt (5.55% per annum in 2025); (iv) impose penalties under arts. 191-193 Ley 58/2003 — for an infracción grave, a penalty of 50%-150% of the omitted amount (100%-150% when false documentation is used), plus enforcement surcharges of 5%-20% in the apremio phase. Where the amount defrauded exceeds 120,000 EUR, criminal prosecution under art. 305 Código Penal may follow (1-5 years imprisonment and a fine of 2-6 times the defrauded amount), together with corporate criminal liability for the SL under art. 310 bis CP. The statute of limitation is 4 years from the end of the voluntary filing period (arts. 66-67 LGT); the exporter bears the burden of proving physical exit from the EU and must preserve the full documentation bundle for at least 5 years.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is an euro-area Member State with full capital and current account convertibility under Article 63 TFEU and the Spanish Law on Foreign Investment and its implementing regulations. The euro is freely convertible; no general central-bank approval is required for inward capital contributions, dividend remittances, royalty payments, or repayment of foreign loans. The remaining controls are limited to statistical declarations and balance-of-payments reporting for transactions exceeding EUR 50,000, EU/UN/OFAC sanctions compliance, AML/CFT controls, foreign-investment screening for critical sectors under Royal Decree-Law 8/2020, and non-resident income tax (IRNR) compliance on distributions.

Export proceeds surrender rules

There is no statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no forced repatriation deadline for export proceeds in Spain. Export collections may be held in EUR or foreign currency accounts in Spanish banks or abroad. For balance-of-payments statistics, export receipts equal to or greater than EUR 50,000 must be reported to Banco de España through the Spanish reporting bank on the relevant periodic declaration; the exporter must retain underlying invoices, customs declarations (DUA), transport documents, and proof of receipt. The practical statutory timeline is the reporting period applicable to each bank's balance-of-payments return, generally monthly or quarterly, rather than a same-day surrender deadline.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem and supervised by the European Central Bank for prudential purposes; foreign-exchange and international-investment statistical control is coordinated with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOMER) within the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Commerce and Business.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium/Low as exclusive treasury bank; High as a supplemental SEPA collection and payment gateway. A fintech EMI authorised under PSD2 and passported into Spain may be registered with Banco de España and can lawfully execute payments, FX conversion, and e-money transactions, but it remains a payment institution rather than a credit institution, so it cannot accept repayable deposits, hold client funds as a core commercial banking service, issue documentary credits, or open a capital-escrow account in the manner of a full Spanish bank. Offshore EMIs outside the EEA face additional legal constraints under Spanish AML law and are generally not acceptable as the primary treasury cloud for a high-risk pharmaceutical manufacturer; if used at all, they should be limited to non-core subthreshold payments through a supervised EU licensee with a letter of no-objection from Banco de España.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Applicant is a newly formed Spanish SL in GMP pharmaceutical manufacturing with non-EU shareholding and no local operating track record.

Root cause: Applicant is a newly formed Spanish SL in GMP pharmaceutical manufacturing with non-EU shareholding and no local operating track record.

Defense evidence: Current Registro Mercantil certificate, AEMPS manufacturing or import authorisation for insulin products, lease or ownership of physical premises, payroll and substance documentation, audited opening balance sheet, board resolution appointing local management, detailed business plan, and licences for the target ISIC scope.
UBO chain includes offshore companies, trusts, or foundations in an opaque jurisdiction.

Root cause: UBO chain includes offshore companies, trusts, or foundations in an opaque jurisdiction.

Defense evidence: Spanish UBO certificate, corporate structure chart with ownership percentages, notarised trust deed or foundation deed, source-of-wealth statement, independent legal opinion on beneficial ownership, and confirmations of the economic purpose of each entity in the chain.
Inbound capital injection appears as a rapid movement of funds from a partner in a higher-risk Latin American jurisdiction.

Root cause: Inbound capital injection appears as a rapid movement of funds from a partner in a higher-risk Latin American jurisdiction.

Defense evidence: Origin-bank account statements, notarised capital increase deed, share-subscription agreement, source-of-funds declaration, audited financial statements or tax returns of the transferor, and a documented commercial rationale for the investment.
Trade collections and documentary letter of credit flows involve high-risk pharmaceutical/TBML exposure with intermediaries in third countries.

Root cause: Trade collections and documentary letter of credit flows involve high-risk pharmaceutical/TBML exposure with intermediaries in third countries.

Defense evidence: Original supply/purchase contracts, UCP600-compliant LC documents, commercial invoices, duty-paid customs declarations (DUA), bills of lading or airway bills, inspection certificates, warehouse receipts, and identity/UBO records of the trade counterparties.
Name-based sanctions or PEP screening generates a hit due to shared names with politically exposed persons or listed entities.

Root cause: Name-based sanctions or PEP screening generates a hit due to shared names with politically exposed persons or listed entities.

Defense evidence: Clean-screen adjudication memo, identity document verification, confirmation of nationality and residency, enhanced due diligence questionnaire, negative news research, sanctions-screening report, and sign-off from the AML compliance officer and where necessary the board risk committee.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Inbound equity must be wired via SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV to a Spanish-based account using the beneficiary IBAN (ES checksum + 20 digits) and BIC, with field 70 stating the ISO 20022 purpose code accepted by the receiving bank (e.g., EQUI for equity contribution, INTC for intra-group funding) and referencing the notarised capital increase deed. The same wire should be supported by the Spanish public deed elevating capital, registration in the Mercantile Registry, Banco de España balance-of-payments declaration where applicable, and, if the investor is non-EU in the health/pharma/critical sector, a prior-authorisation assessment under Royal Decree-Law 8/2020. The receiving bank will verify the corporate signatories, UBO registry, tax ID (CIF/NIF), and the economic substance evidence before releasing funds to the fully operational account.Use TARGET2 for high-value euro settlement, SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for euro payments to EU/EEA beneficiaries, and SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV for all non-euro or non-EEA payments. For commercial trade contracts with Latin American buyers/suppliers, open or receive letters of credit through SWIFT MT700/MT707 under UCP600, advise negotiation/acceptance via MT754/MT756, and settle reimbursements through the issuing bank's correspondent rail or Eurosystem TARGET2 account. Additional clearing options include bank-hosted trade finance portals, SWIFT GPI real-time payment tracking, and escrow-backed LC disbursements where sovereign health procurement requires definitive security.Deliverable Outright FX Forward (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and liquid LATAM EMFX pairs) under an ISDA/FBF Master AgreementNon-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for illiquid or restricted Latin American currencies such as the Argentine peso, with cash settlement in EUR/USDFX Swap (simultaneous spot and forward exchange) for efficient short-term funding of working capitalCross-Currency Swap (CCS) with exchange of principal and interest for medium-term balance-sheet hedging of USD/LATAM debt or receivables

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium/Low as exclusive treasury bank; High as a supplemental SEPA collection and payment gateway. A fintech EMI authorised under PSD2 and passported into Spain may be registered with Banco de España and can lawfully execute payments, FX conversion, and e-money transactions, but it remains a payment institution rather than a credit institution, so it cannot accept repayable deposits, hold client funds as a core commercial banking service, issue documentary credits, or open a capital-escrow account in the manner of a full Spanish bank. Offshore EMIs outside the EEA face additional legal constraints under Spanish AML law and are generally not acceptable as the primary treasury cloud for a high-risk pharmaceutical manufacturer; if used at all, they should be limited to non-core subthreshold payments through a supervised EU licensee with a letter of no-objection from Banco de España.

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% (domestic rate for non-residents; 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if holding ≥5% for 12 months)

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

The 25th day following the 6 months after the end of the tax year (e.g., for calendar year-end, by July 25)

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 Taxable base (Base imponible) Report taxable income from Spanish sources, applying arm's length principles and any applicable tax treaty provisions. Late filing penalties: 5% of tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% after 12 months, plus late payment interest. Additionally, a fine of €1,000 per data item for incorrect or omitted data.
Box 2 Tax rate (Tipo de gravamen) Apply the general 25% rate or the reduced 15% rate if eligible as a new entity; otherwise, apply any special regime. Late filing penalties: 5% of tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% after 12 months, plus late payment interest. Additionally, a fine of €1,000 per data item for incorrect or omitted data.
Box 3 Tax payable (Cuota íntegra) Calculate the gross tax liability before credits and deductions. Late filing penalties: 5% of tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% after 12 months, plus late payment interest. Additionally, a fine of €1,000 per data item for incorrect or omitted data.
Box 4 Deductions and credits (Deducciones y bonificaciones) Apply R&D tax credits, double taxation relief, and other eligible incentives; ensure documentation is retained. Late filing penalties: 5% of tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% after 12 months, plus late payment interest. Additionally, a fine of €1,000 per data item for incorrect or omitted data.
Box 5 Net tax payable (Cuota líquida) Final tax due after all credits and deductions; if negative, indicate refund claim. Late filing penalties: 5% of tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% after 12 months, plus late payment interest. Additionally, a fine of €1,000 per data item for incorrect or omitted data.
Box 6 Withholdings and payments on account (Retenciones y pagos a cuenta) Report any withholdings on income and quarterly installment payments made during the year. Late filing penalties: 5% of tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% after 12 months, plus late payment interest. Additionally, a fine of €1,000 per data item for incorrect or omitted data.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: €10 million net turnover for Local File; €50 million group consolidated turnover for Master File

Economic substance scope: Spain applies general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) and requires economic substance for tax residency. The company must have adequate personnel, premises, and functions to support its activities; otherwise, it may be deemed a shell and denied treaty benefits.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Penalties up to 150% of the tax evaded, plus interest; criminal liability for fraud exceeding €120,000 may lead to imprisonment of 1-6 years.

Director personal liability: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; may face civil restitution, travel bans, and disqualification.
Shell Company

Statutory sanction: Reclassification as a tax haven entity, denial of treaty benefits, and penalties up to 150% of tax avoided; potential criminal charges for fraud.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for taxes and penalties if they are the de facto managers; may face criminal prosecution and travel bans.
AML (Anti-Money Laundering)

Statutory sanction: Fines up to €5 million or 10% of annual turnover for serious breaches; criminal liability for money laundering with imprisonment up to 6 years.

Director personal liability: Directors can be held personally liable for AML failures, including fines and imprisonment if they knowingly or negligently facilitate money laundering.
